observation_text: Child was waiting for their turn at the playground when they jumped in front of another child.
behavior: Jumped in front of another child at the slide.
consequence: Child was reminded to wait and took a turn after.
caregiver_response: Reinforced the importance of taking turns
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage waiting in other situations?
general_support_idea: Use visual timers to help understand wait times.

observation_text: Child was sitting at a table during snack time and took a cracker from a friend's plate.
behavior: Took a cracker from a friend's plate without asking.
consequence: Child returned the cracker and apologized.
caregiver_response: Discussed with the child about asking before taking.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help remind them to ask?
general_support_idea: Practice sharing games to build understanding.

observation_text: Child was playing with a toy in a group and began to grab it from another child.
behavior: Grabbed a toy from another child.
consequence: Child was guided to ask for a turn instead.
possible_trigger: Desire to play with the toy
emotion_context: Wants to play with it first
caregiver_response: Encouraged them to ask politely for a turn.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use to promote sharing in play?
general_support_idea: Role-play asking for turns during play time.

observation_text: Child was waiting for their turn to speak during a group activity and began to fidget.
behavior: Started to fidget and make noise while waiting.
consequence: Child was reminded to use a quiet hand signal to indicate they were ready.
caregiver_response: Promoted the use of a hand signal for waiting.
suggested_followup_question: What can help them while they wait?
general_support_idea: Introduce a talking stick during discussions.

observation_text: Child was playing a board game with friends and interrupted frequently.
behavior: Interrupted friends while they were taking turns.
consequence: Child agreed to wait for their turn after reminders.
caregiver_response: Reinforced the value of waiting and listening.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make the game more enjoyable for everyone?
general_support_idea: Set a timer for each turn during games.

observation_text: Child was waiting at a restaurant for a meal and started to get restless.
behavior: Started to wiggle in the seat and make noise.
consequence: Child calmed down after playing a game on the menu.
caregiver_response: Engaged the child in a wait-time activity.
suggested_followup_question: What activities can we do to pass the time?
general_support_idea: Bring small toys or games to keep busy while waiting.

observation_text: Child was waiting to play a game on the tablet and insisted on going first.
antecedent: Waiting to use a shared tablet
behavior: Insisted loudly that they wanted to go first.
consequence: Child took a deep breath and agreed to wait for their turn.
caregiver_response: Promoted patience and rewarded waiting with a fun game.
suggested_followup_question: How can we support them in waiting for their turn?
general_support_idea: Make a visual schedule of turn-taking.

observation_text: Child was at the park and ran ahead to the swings without waiting for their brother.
behavior: Ran ahead to play on the swings.
consequence: Child was reminded to stay close and wait for their brother.
caregiver_response: Emphasized the importance of staying together.
suggested_followup_question: How can we reinforce staying close in busy places?
general_support_idea: Use a buddy system where they look out for each other.

observation_text: Child was involved in a group game and kept cutting in line.
behavior: Cut into the line during a game.
consequence: Child was asked to step back and wait their turn again.
caregiver_response: Encouraged patience and cooperation among peers.
suggested_followup_question: What can help them understand waiting?
general_support_idea: Discuss the benefits of fairness in games.

observation_text: Child was playing at a friend's house and refused to share a toy during playtime.
behavior: Held onto a toy and did not let friends take turns.
consequence: Child handed the toy to a friend after discussion.
possible_trigger: Desiring to play with the toy first
caregiver_response: Encouraged them to take turns with explanations.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage sharing in playdates?
general_support_idea: Model sharing by taking turns with toys.

observation_text: Child was in the store and ran ahead to the toy section.
behavior: Ran ahead excitedly to look at toys.
consequence: Child was called back and reminded to walk together.
emotion_context: In a hurry to see toys
caregiver_response: Reinforced the need to stay close in stores.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use to keep them close?
general_support_idea: Identify toy areas before shopping to plan ahead.

observation_text: Child was at a birthday party and kept grabbing balloons from others.
behavior: Kept reaching for balloons from other children.
consequence: Child was reminded to wait and ask before grabbing.
caregiver_response: Discussed sharing and waiting in party games.
suggested_followup_question: How can we practice waiting in group settings?
general_support_idea: Incorporate sharing rules into games.

observation_text: Child was at the playground and wanted to go down the slide first.
antecedent: Seeing friends take turns on the slide
behavior: Ran to the slide and jumped in front of a friend.
consequence: Child was reminded to wait their turn and counted to five.
caregiver_response: Reinforced the concept of taking turns with a countdown.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make waiting fun?
general_support_idea: Use timers or fun countdowns to wait.

observation_text: Child was waiting to board the bus and stepped away from the group.
behavior: Stepped away to look at something interesting across the street.
consequence: Child was called back to stay with the group.
caregiver_response: Discussed the importance of staying close in busy areas.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help them stay focused?
general_support_idea: Talk about staying safe in public places.

observation_text: Child was at the playground and kept moving away from the play area.
behavior: Left the play area to explore alone.
consequence: Child was stopped and asked to return to safety.
caregiver_response: Guided child back, discussing the importance of staying close.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage safe exploration?
general_support_idea: Set boundaries on where they can explore.

observation_text: Child was at the park and refused to leave the swings after being called.
behavior: Ignored requests and continued swinging.
consequence: Child finally got off when promised a fun activity next.
caregiver_response: Provided a fun incentive to leave.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make transitions smoother?
general_support_idea: Use visuals for activities and transitions.

observation_text: Child was waiting to eat at a restaurant and began to pull on the tablecloth.
behavior: Pulled on the tablecloth, causing items to slide off.
consequence: Child was reminded to keep hands to themselves and play quietly.
caregiver_response: Redirected to draw on the napkins.
suggested_followup_question: How can we manage waiting in restaurants?
general_support_idea: Bring crayons and paper for drawing.

observation_text: Child was in a group activity and kept jumping ahead in the line.
behavior: Jumped ahead to grab supplies before others.
consequence: Child was gently reminded to wait for their turn.
caregiver_response: Reinforced taking turns with supplies.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use to encourage turn-taking?
general_support_idea: Create a visual queue for turns during activities.

observation_text: Child was in a playgroup and kept interrupting others during storytelling.
behavior: Interrupted with comments and questions before others spoke.
consequence: Child was guided to wait until others finished.
caregiver_response: Promoted taking turns in sharing ideas.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help them practice waiting their turn to speak?
general_support_idea: Use a talking toy to pass around.

observation_text: Child was at a family gathering and kept trying to take snacks from the table.
behavior: Tried to grab snacks before others had a chance.
consequence: Child was reminded to wait for everyone to be served first.
caregiver_response: Reinforced the importance of waiting for turns at family events.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to teach patience at meals?
general_support_idea: Establish a waiting rule for snacks during gatherings.

observation_text: During snack time, child waited patiently for their turn to pick a snack from the bowl.
behavior: Child raised their hand to signal they wanted a turn.
consequence: Child took a piece of fruit after their turn was called.
caregiver_response: Encouraged child to keep waiting patiently.
suggested_followup_question: What snacks do you want to try next time?
general_support_idea: Praise children for waiting their turn during group activities.

observation_text: On the playground, child watched peers play on the swings.
antecedent: Other children were swinging and laughing.
behavior: Child stood nearby, waiting for a swing to open up.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Suggested they ask a friend to play tag instead.
suggested_followup_question: How did it feel to wait for the swing?
general_support_idea: Encourage children to engage in alternative games while waiting for their turn.

observation_text: At a public restaurant, child wanted to play with the menu instead of waiting for food.
antecedent: Food was taking longer than expected to arrive.
behavior: Child started flipping the menu loudly and fidgeting in their chair.
consequence: Child began to focus on the coloring page after the caregiver suggested it.
caregiver_response: Redirected the child to a fun activity they could do while waiting.
suggested_followup_question: Would a snack make waiting easier?
general_support_idea: Offer quiet activities to help children manage waiting times.

observation_text: While shopping, child suddenly ran ahead to look at a toy display, leaving the caregiver behind.
antecedent: Saw a toy that excited them.
behavior: Child dashed away, ignoring the caregiver’s call to stop.
consequence: Child returned to the caregiver after they called their name multiple times.
caregiver_response: Gently reminded the child about safety in stores.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make sure to stay close next time?
general_support_idea: Discuss boundaries and safety while out together.

observation_text: In the school classroom, child waited for three friends to finish before they could all start a game together.
antecedent: Friends were finishing a task before playtime.
behavior: Child sat quietly at their desk, looking at the clock.
consequence: Child initiated a group discussion about the game as soon as everyone was ready.
caregiver_response: Praised the child for being patient and waiting for everyone.
suggested_followup_question: What game do you think everyone will enjoy?
general_support_idea: Encourage collaboration and patience in group settings.
